items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: a team called Butterbeans and Susie. Well, this wasn't Butterbeans and Susie, but they had a similar type act, and they were using the music of Butterbeans and Susie.

ctx.x: especially if it didn't have the chords written on there, you know. All of the music had the chords and everything that we had to play, except one of the pieces, and that was something that was sort of a team who were imitating one of the very popular acts of that particular time, a team called Butterbeans and Susie. Well, this wasn't Butterbeans and Susie, but they had a similar type act, and they were using the music of Butterbeans and Susie. And this music did not have any chords on it at all. So I didn't know…

Anyway, we made it through the summer. And this kid and I became fast friends, the saxophone player... He was studying with somebody down at the Marine Barracks here in Washington, studying clarinet and saxophone. So in the mornings he would be up early practicing. I forget the name of this book that he had, that he was practicing out of. It was a very popular saxophone or clarinet book. Because I've seen a lot of clarinet players with it. He would sit up, and he'd be running the exercise...
